name: Vacuum sublimation extraction of air from ice-core samples for d13CO2, CO2 and N2O (-34 C vessel, -150 C water trap, LN2 CO2 trap, <2e-7 mbar)
plain_name: Release ancient air from ice-core pieces to measure past CO2
description: A 30 g ice cylinder (3.2 cm diameter, 4.5 cm long) is held at about -34 C in an evacuated glass sublimation vessel and sublimated by infrared halogen lamps; water is removed in traps down to -150 C, CO2/N2O are frozen in a liquid-nitrogen trap and sealed in a glass capillary for GC-IRMS, reconstructing past atmospheric CO2 and its carbon isotopes.
keywords: Release ancient air from ice-core pieces to measure past CO2

sources.citation: Schmitt J, Schneider R, Fischer H (2011). A sublimation technique for high-precision measurements of d13CO2 and mixing ratios of CO2 and N2O from air trapped in ice cores. Atmos. Meas. Tech. 4, 1445-1461. doi:10.5194/amt-4-1445-2011

reported_equipment: Leybold turbo molecular pump backed by a rotary vane vacuum pump
Caburn CF sublimation vessel (33 mm o.d., 121 mm length)

requirements.rationale: The ice sample is held near -34 C (239.15 K) during sublimation, keeping it well below -20 C.
The external water trap must reach -150 C (123.15 K) to reach the required H2O vapour pressure.
Extraction is done in a high-vacuum sublimation line.
A leak-free line reaches below 2e-7 mbar on the high-vacuum side before sampling.
CO2 and N2O are frozen out in a trap immersed in liquid nitrogen.
The ice is trimmed to a 3.2 cm cylinder to fit the 3.3 cm vessel.
The ice piece is 4.5 cm long along the vessel axis.
The ice is sublimated by infrared light from halogen bulbs shining through the glass vessel.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
